title: Encrypted control-plane RPC resilience
intent: Make encrypted NIP-59/ContextVM control-plane RPC fast-failing and observable when a request reaches the Bahia service, without changing terminal truth semantics.
observed_problem: Encrypted gift-wrapped ContextVM requests previously had no early liveness signal.
A routing mismatch or unauthenticated backend relay subscription was indistinguishable from slow work until the blind long timeout expired.
intended_behavior: After wrapper routing and requester authorization pass, and before invoking the registered handler, the backend publishes a gift-wrapped JSON-RPC notification to the requester.
The progress notification shape is {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/progress","params":{"requestId":"<published-request-event-id>","status":"processing"}} and it has no id/result/error.
Routing mismatches remain silent; unauthorized requests keep the existing -32001 terminal error without a progress ack.
System discovery advertises control_plane.capabilities containing encrypted_controlplane.progress_ack and control_plane.wire_version=contextvm-jsonrpc-v2.
The web shared subscription treats progress as ack-only: it clears the short ack timer and waits for terminal result/error.
When the capability is absent, browser clients preserve the legacy single long timeout.
Browser request paths fail before publish when encrypted discovery, service pubkey validity, or connected Bahia relays are absent.
out_of_scope: Fixing the deployment-side silent drop tracked separately by bahia-50b7.
